questions.question: In 2018, Ganesh and Kumaresh Rajagopalan won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Carnatic instrumental music. For playing which instrument did they win this award?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Violin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ganesh and Kumaresh Rajagopalan are renowned Carnatic violinists, celebrated for their exceptional talent and contribution to Indian classical music.
 
• They received the prestigious Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2018 for their mastery of the **violin** in the realm of Carnatic instrumental music.
 
• The duo is known for their innovative style that blends traditional Carnatic music with contemporary elements, appealing to a broad audience.
 
• Ganesh and Kumaresh began their violin journey at a young age, performing their first concert as a duo when they were just children.
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is one of India's highest honors in the performing arts, recognizing outstanding contributions to music, dance, and drama.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Violin in Carnatic Music:**

 
 
• The violin was introduced into Carnatic music in the 19th century and has since become a staple instrument in the genre.
 
• It is typically played in a sitting posture, with the instrument resting on the player's left shoulder, allowing for intricate gamakas (oscillations) unique to Carnatic music.
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi:**
 
 
• Established in 1953, the Sangeet Natak Akademi is India's National Academy for Music, Dance, and Drama, under the Ministry of Culture.
 
• The award, instituted in 1952, is given annually to artists for their outstanding contribution to their respective fields.
 
 
 
• **Role of Violin in Indian Classical Music:**
 
 
• In Carnatic music, the violin is used as both a solo instrument and as an accompaniment to vocal performances.
 
• Its ability to mimic the human voice makes it a perfect choice for rendering the nuances of ragas.
 
 
 
• **Ganesh-Kumaresh Duo:**
 
 
• The brothers are known for their ability to experiment with fusion music while maintaining the essence of Carnatic tradition.
 
• They have performed internationally, showcasing the richness of Indian classical music on global platforms.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is detected by the Widal test?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Typhoid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Widal test** is a serological test used to detect the presence of antibodies against **Salmonella Typhi**, the causative agent of typhoid fever.
 
• It measures agglutination (clumping) of antigens and antibodies in the patient’s serum to diagnose **enteric fever** (typhoid and paratyphoid).
 
• This test identifies the **O (somatic) and H (flagellar)** antigens of Salmonella Typhi and Salmonella Paratyphi.
 
• The Widal test is especially useful in endemic regions where typhoid fever is common.
 
• A significant rise in antibody titers between two samples taken 7–10 days apart confirms active infection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Typhoid Fever:**

 
 
• Typhoid is a bacterial infection caused by **Salmonella Typhi**, transmitted through contaminated food or water.
 
• Symptoms include prolonged fever, abdominal pain, weakness, loss of appetite, and sometimes a rash called "rose spots."
 
• Preventive measures include vaccination, safe drinking water, and proper sanitation.
 
 
 
• **Widal Test Procedure:**
 
 
• The patient’s blood sample is collected, and the serum is separated.
 
• The serum is mixed with antigen suspensions of Salmonella Typhi and observed for agglutination.
 
• A titer of 1:160 or higher is generally considered significant in endemic areas.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of Widal Test:**
 
 
• It may produce false positives due to prior vaccination or cross-reactivity with other infections.
 
• It is less reliable in the early stages of infection as antibody levels take time to rise.
 
 
 
• **Alternate Diagnostic Methods:**
 
 
• Blood culture is the gold standard for diagnosing typhoid fever but requires specialized lab facilities.
 
• Rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) are also available, but their sensitivity and specificity vary.

questions.question: In which language was 'Mudraraksha' play written by Vishakhadatta?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sanskrit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **'Mudraraksha'** is a historical Sanskrit play written by **Vishakhadatta**.
 
• The play is believed to have been written between the **4th and 8th centuries CE**.
 
• It depicts the political and administrative strategies employed during the reign of the **Mauryan Empire**, particularly around the time of **Chandragupta Maurya**.
 
• The narrative revolves around the clever diplomacy of **Chanakya (Kautilya)** to dethrone the Nanda dynasty and establish Chandragupta Maurya as the ruler.
 
• 'Mudraraksha' translates to "The Signet Ring of Rakshasa," referring to the role of Rakshasa, the loyal minister of the Nanda dynasty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sanskrit Literature:**

 
 
• Sanskrit is one of the oldest languages in the world and forms the basis of classical Indian literature.
 
• It has a rich tradition of plays, poetry, epics, and philosophical texts like the Vedas, Upanishads, and epics like Mahabharata and Ramayana.
 
 
 
• **Chanakya:**
 
 
• Also known as Kautilya or Vishnugupta, he was a celebrated strategist and the author of the treatise **Arthashastra**.
 
• He played a pivotal role in the establishment of the Mauryan Empire.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context of 'Mudraraksha':**
 
 
• The play provides insight into the political dynamics and strategies used during ancient Indian history.
 
• It highlights themes of loyalty, power, and statecraft.
 
 
 
• **Mauryan Empire:**
 
 
• The Mauryan Empire (322–185 BCE) was one of the largest empires in ancient India, founded by Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• It reached its peak under Emperor Ashoka, known for his propagation of Buddhism and the Edicts of Ashoka.

questions.question: What does M stand for in BHIM-UPI?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Money**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• BHIM stands for **Bharat Interface for Money**, a mobile application developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).
 
• The letter **M** in BHIM-UPI stands for "Money," emphasizing the app's primary purpose of facilitating secure and instant monetary transactions.
 
• BHIM app leverages the **Unified Payments Interface (UPI)**, a system enabling real-time interbank transactions using a mobile device.
 
• It was launched by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** on **30th December 2016**, as part of India's push towards a cashless economy.
 
• The app ensures ease of use and accessibility, allowing users to send or receive money using a **UPI ID or QR code**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Unified Payments Interface (UPI):**

 
 
• UPI is a **real-time payment system** developed by NPCI that facilitates instant fund transfer between two bank accounts via mobile devices.
 
• It eliminates the need for cumbersome details like IFSC codes or account numbers, using a **unique UPI ID** for transactions.
 
 
 
• **Features of BHIM App:**
 
 
• Supports transactions via **UPI ID, mobile number, or QR code**.
 
• Allows linking multiple bank accounts and offers a seamless user interface.
 
• Provides additional features such as checking balance and generating transaction history.
 
 
 
• **NPCI:**
 
 
• The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) is an organization responsible for managing India's retail payment systems.
 
• It oversees UPI, IMPS, RuPay card network, and other payment systems.
 
 
 
• **QR Code Payments:**
 
 
• QR codes in BHIM allow users to scan and pay instantly without sharing sensitive details.
 
• This feature enhances security and ease of use in monetary transactions.

questions.question: As per Census 2011, what is the literacy rate of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.7404**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per Census 2011, the literacy rate of India is **74.04%**, which marks a significant improvement from the previous Census 2001 literacy rate of 64.83%.
 
• The male literacy rate stands at **82.14%**, while the female literacy rate is **65.46%**, indicating a gender gap in literacy.
 
• Kerala has the highest literacy rate at **94%**, while Bihar recorded the lowest literacy rate at **61.8%**.
 
• The total number of literates in India as per Census 2011 is approximately **778.45 million**, with 434.77 million males and 343.68 million females.
 
• India's literacy rate is calculated for the population aged **7 years and above**, based on the ability to read and write with understanding.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Definition of Literacy:**

 
 
• As per Census 2011, a person aged 7 years and above who can both read and write with understanding in any language is considered literate.
 
 
 
• **Census 2011 Overview:**
 
 
• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
• Census 2011 was the 15th Census of India and the 7th since Independence.
 
 
 
• **Literacy and Development:**
 
 
• Higher literacy rates are directly associated with socio-economic development, employment opportunities, and poverty reduction.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives to Improve Literacy:**
 
 
• Programs like **Saakshar Bharat**, **Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan**, and **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao** aim to enhance literacy levels, especially among women and marginalized communities.

questions.question: Constipation could be a sign that the person in suffering from a lack of ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dietary Fibre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dietary fibre is essential for maintaining a healthy digestive system and aids in regular bowel movements by increasing stool bulk.
 
• A lack of dietary fibre can lead to constipation, as the body struggles to efficiently pass stool through the intestines.
 
• Sources of dietary fibre include fruits (e.g., apples, bananas), vegetables (e.g., broccoli, carrots), whole grains (e.g., oats, brown rice), legumes, and seeds.
 
• The recommended daily intake of fibre for adults is approximately 25-30 grams, depending on gender and age, according to global health standards.
 
• Dietary fibre also helps regulate blood sugar levels and cholesterol, making it beneficial for overall health beyond digestion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Dietary Fibre:**

 
 
• **Soluble fibre:** Dissolves in water and forms a gel-like substance; found in oats, apples, and beans.
 
• **Insoluble fibre:** Does not dissolve in water; helps add bulk to stool; found in whole grains, nuts, and vegetables.
 
 
 
• **Constipation:** A condition where bowel movements are infrequent or hard to pass, often caused by insufficient fibre intake, dehydration, or lack of physical activity.
 
• **Health Benefits of Fibre:** In addition to preventing constipation, fibre helps reduce the risk of heart disease, type 2 diabetes, and certain types of cancer.
 
• **Sources of Fibre:** Whole foods such as fruits, vegetables, legumes, nuts, seeds, and whole grains are rich in dietary fibre. Processed and refined foods generally have lower fibre content.
 
• **Tips to Increase Fibre Intake:** Gradually incorporate fibre-rich foods into your diet, drink plenty of water, and avoid excessive consumption of processed foods.

questions.question: The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution are borrowed from which country's constitution?

options.text: The Constitution of the United States
The Constitution of the United Kingdom
The Constitution of the Soviet Union

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Constitution of Ireland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution are inspired by the **Irish Constitution (1937)**.
 
• These principles were included in the Indian Constitution to establish a framework for achieving socio-economic justice and guiding state policy.
 
• The Irish model was particularly influential in shaping the concept of **non-justiciable rights**, ensuring that these principles serve as guidelines rather than enforceable laws.
 
• Part IV (Articles 36 to 51) of the Indian Constitution contains the Directive Principles of State Policy, emphasizing ideals such as **social welfare, economic equality, and justice.**
 
• The framers of the Indian Constitution, including Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, recognized the importance of borrowing this concept from Ireland to address India’s socio-economic challenges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy:**

 
 
• These principles are **non-justiciable**, meaning they are not legally enforceable by courts but are fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• They aim to establish a welfare state by addressing issues such as **health, education, livelihood, and social justice.**
 
• Examples include promoting equal pay for equal work, protecting children and women, and ensuring the right to work and education.
 
 
 
• **Influence of Ireland:**
 
 
• The Irish Constitution (1937) was drafted under the leadership of Éamon de Valera and included directives for social and economic justice.
 
• India adopted similar provisions to encourage state action for societal welfare.
 
 
 
• **Key Articles in Part IV:**
 
 
• Article 39(b): Distribution of resources to serve the common good.
 
• Article 41: Right to work, education, and public assistance.
 
• Article 44: Uniform Civil Code for all citizens.
 
 
 
• **Relationship with Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• While Fundamental Rights are enforceable, Directive Principles act as complementary provisions to achieve a balance between individual freedoms and collective welfare.
 
• The Supreme Court has often emphasized the harmonious interpretation of Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles.

questions.question: In which of the following years did Lord Curzon announce the partition of Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1905**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lord Curzon, the then Viceroy of India, announced the **Partition of Bengal** on **July 19, 1905**, and it was implemented on **October 16, 1905**.
 
• The partition was aimed at dividing Bengal into two provinces: **Eastern Bengal and Assam**, with a Muslim majority, and **West Bengal**, with a Hindu majority.
 
• The official reason given was to improve administrative efficiency in the large and populous Bengal province, which had a population of over 78 million at the time.
 
• The partition led to widespread protests and marked the beginning of the **Swadeshi Movement** (1905-1911), a significant phase in India's struggle for independence.
 
• Due to severe opposition and unrest, the partition was annulled in **1911** by the British government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swadeshi Movement:**

 
 
• Launched in response to the Partition of Bengal, this movement emphasized the use of indigenous goods and boycotting British products.
 
• It saw the rise of nationalist leaders like **Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Lala Lajpat Rai**.
 
• Key cultural aspects, such as nationalistic songs like *"Vande Mataram,"* became symbols of resistance.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Challenges:**
 
 
• Bengal was the largest province in British India, making governance difficult, which was cited as the primary reason for partition.
 
• However, critics argued that the real motive was to create religious division and weaken the growing nationalist movement.
 
 
 
• **Reversal of Partition:**
 
 
• In 1911, the British annulled the partition due to the sustained opposition and shifted the capital of British India from **Calcutta to Delhi**.
 
• The annulment is considered a partial victory for Indian nationalists, though it did not eliminate British control.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Indian Nationalism:**
 
 
• The partition and subsequent unrest significantly contributed to the growth of the Indian National Congress and the demand for **Swaraj (self-rule)**.
 
• It also led to the unification of Indian leaders across regions and religions to oppose British policies.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a qualification/eligibility to become the President of India?

options.text: Must be a citizen of India
Must be qualified for election as a member of the house of the people
Must have completed the age of thirty-five years
Must hold any office of profit

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The President of India must **not hold any office of profit** under the Government of India, State Government, or any other public authority while contesting the election.
 
• Qualifications to become the President of India include:
 
 
• **Being a citizen of India**.
 
• **Being qualified** to be elected as a member of the Lok Sabha (House of the People).
 
• **Attaining the age of 35 years** or more.
 
 
 
• The office of profit clause is meant to ensure **independence and impartiality** of the position of the President.
 
• Holding an office of profit disqualifies a candidate as it creates a potential conflict of interest.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Office of Profit:**

 
 
• An office of profit refers to a position that yields financial gain, advantage, or benefit.
 
• The concept ensures separation of powers and prevents legislators from holding executive positions that may influence their decisions.
 
 
 
• **Election Process of the President:**
 
 
• The President is elected by an **Electoral College** comprising elected members of both Houses of Parliament and Legislative Assemblies of States and Union Territories.
 
• The election is conducted using a proportional representation system with a single transferable vote.
 
 
 
• **Term and Role of the President:**
 
 
• The President serves for a term of **five years** but is eligible for re-election.
 
• The President is the **constitutional head** of the state and acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
 
 
 
• **Disqualifications for the Presidency:**
 
 
• Being an undischarged insolvent.
 
• Having an unsound mind as declared by a competent court.
 
• Holding an office of profit under the Government of India or any state government.

questions.question: Losoong festival is predominantly celebrated in Sikkim by which of the following tribes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhutia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Losoong** is a significant festival predominantly celebrated by the **Bhutia tribe** in the Indian state of Sikkim.
 
• The festival marks the **New Year of the Sikkimese Bhutia community** as per the Tibetan lunar calendar and is celebrated in the month of December.
 
• It is also known as the **Harvest Festival**, symbolizing the end of the harvesting season and the beginning of a new year.
 
• Cultural activities like **traditional Cham dances** (mask dances by monks) are performed in monasteries, including the famous **Phodong and Rumtek monasteries**.
 
• The festival emphasizes **community bonding** and includes rituals to ensure prosperity, good harvests, and well-being for the coming year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhutia Tribe:**

 
 
• The Bhutias are a prominent tribal community in Sikkim, originally of Tibetan descent.
 
• Their language, **Sikkimese** (a dialect of Tibetan), and customs are deeply influenced by Tibetan Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Cham Dance:**
 
 
• A sacred ritual dance performed by monks during festivals like Losoong, featuring colorful masks and costumes.
 
• It represents mythical stories and serves as a medium to ward off evil spirits.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Losoong:**
 
 
• The festival is a time for expressing gratitude for the harvest and praying for future prosperity.
 
• It serves as a cultural identity marker for the Bhutia community and promotes tourism in Sikkim.
 
 
 
• **Other Tribes in Sikkim:**
 
 
• Besides Bhutias, other major tribes in Sikkim include the **Lepchas** and **Nepalis**.
 
• Each tribe has its unique festivals, traditions, and cultural practices.

questions.question: Which is the largest agro-based industry of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cotton textile industry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The cotton textile industry is the **largest agro-based industry in India**, contributing significantly to employment and exports.
 
• India is the **largest producer of cotton** globally and has a robust supply chain for cotton textiles.
 
• The cotton textile sector accounts for approximately **14% of industrial production** and contributes around **30% of India's total export earnings**.
 
• This industry plays a crucial role in the Indian economy by employing about **35 million people**, making it one of the largest sources of employment.
 
• Major production centers include **Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Punjab**, among others.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agro-based industries:** Industries that derive raw materials from agricultural products, such as cotton, sugarcane, jute, and tea.
 
• **Textile industry in India:** India’s textile industry is divided into organized (mills) and unorganized (handlooms, power looms) sectors, with cotton being its backbone.
 
• **Export significance:** Cotton textiles are one of the largest contributors to India's export basket, particularly to the United States, European Union, and Middle Eastern countries.
 
• **Government initiatives:** Schemes like **Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme (TUFS)** and **National Textile Policy** aim to modernize and boost the cotton textile sector.
 
• **Challenges:** The industry faces issues such as fluctuating cotton prices, competition from synthetic fibers, and global trade dynamics.

questions.question: Which of the following dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate finally annexed Jaunpur into the empire of Delhi Sultanate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lodi dynasty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Lodi dynasty**, under Sikandar Lodi, annexed Jaunpur into the Delhi Sultanate in 1494.
 
• Jaunpur had been an independent sultanate established after the disintegration of the Tughlaq dynasty but was brought back under Delhi's control during Sikandar Lodi’s reign.
 
• Sikandar Lodi pursued aggressive expansion policies and sought to consolidate territories lost during earlier dynasties.
 
• The annexation of Jaunpur strengthened the Lodi dynasty’s influence in northern India and ensured the unification of key territories under the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• Jaunpur became an important administrative and cultural center under Sikandar Lodi after its reintegration into the Delhi Sultanate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lodi Dynasty Overview:**

 
 
• The Lodi dynasty (1451–1526) was the last dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate and was founded by Bahlul Lodi.
 
• Sikandar Lodi (r. 1489–1517) was one of the most prominent rulers of the dynasty, known for his administrative reforms and military campaigns.
 
 
 
• **Jaunpur Sultanate:**
 
 
• The Jaunpur Sultanate was established by Malik Sarwar, a former governor of the Tughlaq dynasty, in 1394.
 
• It flourished as a center of learning and culture, earning the nickname "Shiraz of India" during its independence.
 
 
 
• **Sikandar Lodi’s Achievements:**
 
 
• He reorganized tax administration and promoted agriculture to strengthen the economy.
 
• He was a patron of Persian culture and literature, further enriching the intellectual landscape of his era.
 
 
 
• **Delhi Sultanate:**
 
 
• The Delhi Sultanate was a Muslim kingdom based in Delhi that ruled large parts of the Indian subcontinent from 1206 to 1526.
 
• It saw five major dynasties: the Mamluk, Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, and Lodi dynasties.
 
 
 
• **Decline of the Lodi Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Lodi dynasty ended in 1526 when Ibrahim Lodi was defeated by Babur at the First Battle of Panipat, leading to the establishment of the Mughal Empire.

questions.question: The property by virtue of which carbon can form a C-C covalent bond is called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**catenation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Catenation** is the ability of an atom to form covalent bonds with other atoms of the same element, enabling the formation of chains, rings, or networks.
 
• **Carbon** exhibits exceptional catenation due to its ability to form strong C-C single bonds and a wide variety of complex structures.
 
• The high bond energy of the C-C bond contributes to its stability, allowing carbon to form long chains and complex molecules.
 
• Catenation is not unique to carbon but is most prominently observed in carbon due to its small atomic size and tetravalency.
 
• Elements like **silicon** and **sulfur** also exhibit catenation, but to a lesser degree compared to carbon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tetravalency:** Carbon has four valence electrons, allowing it to form four covalent bonds with other atoms or molecules.
 
• **Allotropy:** Carbon exists in different structural forms (allotropes) like diamond, graphite, and fullerenes, due to variations in bonding and arrangement of atoms.
 
• **Covalency:** Covalency refers to the number of covalent bonds an element can form. Carbon’s covalency is 4, leading to versatile bonding capabilities.
 
• **Hydrocarbons:** Catenation enables the formation of hydrocarbons, which are compounds consisting solely of carbon and hydrogen atoms.
 
• **Applications:** The ability of carbon to form long chains and rings is fundamental to organic chemistry and the synthesis of biomolecules, polymers, and industrial compounds.

questions.question: ______ received Padma Shri 2017 award for being an exponent of Nagpuri folk dance Jhumar.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mukund Nayak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mukund Nayak** received the **Padma Shri award in 2017** for his significant contributions to the promotion of the Nagpuri folk dance "Jhumar."
 
• He is a renowned **folk artist, singer, and writer** from Jharkhand who has played a pivotal role in preserving the cultural heritage of the state.
 
• Jhumar is a traditional tribal dance, and Mukund Nayak has been instrumental in its revival and propagation on national and international platforms.
 
• His efforts have brought recognition to the Nagpuri folk traditions, ensuring they are passed down to future generations.
 
• As a cultural ambassador, Mukund Nayak has also worked to preserve tribal art forms like **Chhau dance** and tribal music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Padma Shri Award:**

 
 
• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award in India, instituted in **1954**.
 
• It is awarded to individuals for their distinguished contributions in various fields, such as arts, education, literature, sports, medicine, and social service.
 
 
 
• **Jhumar Dance:**
 
 
• Jhumar is a traditional folk dance of the tribal communities in **Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha**.
 
• It is performed during harvest seasons or festive occasions and involves rhythmic movements to the beats of traditional instruments like the **Mandar and Nagara**.
 
 
 
• **Chhau Dance:**
 
 
• Chhau is a semi-classical Indian dance with tribal origins, recognized by UNESCO as an **Intangible Cultural Heritage** of Humanity.
 
• It is traditionally performed in regions of Jharkhand, West Bengal, and Odisha, blending martial, tribal, and folk elements.
 
 
 
• **Folk Traditions of Jharkhand:**
 
 
• Jharkhand is home to a rich variety of folk music, dance, and art forms rooted in tribal culture, including **Paika, Jhumar, Domkach, and Phagua.**
 
• These traditions play a significant role in preserving the tribal identity and are celebrated during festivals and community events.

questions.question: Who wrote the novel 'The Catcher in the Rye'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**JD Salinger**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **J.D. Salinger** (Jerome David Salinger) is the author of the novel **'The Catcher in the Rye,'** published in **1951.**
 
• The book is considered a classic of **modern American literature** and has been included in numerous "must-read" lists worldwide.
 
• 'The Catcher in the Rye' follows the story of **Holden Caulfield,** a disillusioned teenager navigating alienation and rebellion in postwar America.
 
• The novel became famous for its **controversial themes** such as teenage angst, identity, and mental health, which resonated with young readers.
 
• Salinger became reclusive after the novel's success, withdrawing from public life and publishing very little thereafter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **J.D. Salinger:**

 
 
• Born on **January 1, 1919**, in New York City, and died on **January 27, 2010.**
 
• Besides 'The Catcher in the Rye,' Salinger also published works like **'Nine Stories'** (1953), **'Franny and Zooey'** (1961), and **'Raise High the Roof Beam, Carpenters and Seymour: An Introduction'** (1963).
 
• His writing style is often described as **minimalist** and deeply introspective, with a focus on complex characters.
 
 
 
• **The Catcher in the Rye:**
 
 
• The novel's title refers to Holden's fantasy of being a "catcher" who saves children from falling into adulthood's corruption.
 
• It has been translated into multiple languages and sold over **65 million copies worldwide.**
 
 
 
• **Holden Caulfield:**
 
 
• The protagonist is a symbol of teenage rebellion, and his narrative voice is characterized by sarcasm and vulnerability.
 
• He deals with themes of **identity, alienation, and the loss of innocence.**
 
 
 
• **Controversy:**
 
 
• The novel was banned in many schools and libraries due to its use of profanity and exploration of controversial subjects like **mental health, sexuality, and societal hypocrisy.**
 
• Despite this, it remains one of the most studied and discussed novels in literature courses.

• England won the ICC Cricket World Cup 2019 by defeating New Zealand in the final at **Lords** in a dramatic **Super Over**, marking their first-ever World Cup title.
 
• The tournament featured **48 matches**, with **Ben Stokes** playing a pivotal role in England's victory, earning him the title of **Player of the Match in the final**.
 
• The event was jointly organized by the **England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB)** under the governance of the International Cricket Council (ICC).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The **2011 ICC Cricket World Cup** was co-hosted by **India, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh**.
 
• The **2015 ICC Cricket World Cup** was jointly hosted by **Australia and New Zealand**.
 
• The **2007 ICC Cricket World Cup** was hosted by **West Indies**.
 
 
 
• **Round-Robin Format:**
 
 
• In this format, each team plays against all other teams once.
 
• The top four teams based on points qualify for the knockout stage.
 
 
 
• **Super Over:**
 
 
• A tie-breaking method used in limited-overs cricket when a match ends in a tie.
 
• Each team bats for one over (6 balls), and the team with the most runs wins.
 
 
 
• **Key Players in 2019 World Cup Final:**
 
 
• **Ben Stokes:** Instrumental in England's win with an unbeaten 84 runs in the final.
 
• **Jofra Archer:** Bowled the decisive Super Over for England.

• The 2019 victory marked **England's maiden ICC Men's Cricket World Cup title** after several near misses in previous editions.

questions.question: The Panchpatmali mineral deposit region is located in which state from the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2 - Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Panchpatmali mineral deposit region is located in the **Koraput district** of Odisha, India.
 
• It is known for its **bauxite reserves**, which are among the largest in India.
 
• The bauxite deposits at Panchpatmali are mined by **National Aluminium Company Limited (NALCO)**, a Navratna CPSE under the Ministry of Mines.
 
• The Panchpatmali mines consist of two plateaus: the **South Panchpatmali** and the **North Panchpatmali**.
 
• This region plays a critical role in the production of **alumina and aluminium**, contributing significantly to India's industrial sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bauxite:**

 
 
• Bauxite is the primary ore of aluminium and is composed mainly of aluminium oxide minerals.
 
• It is typically formed in tropical and subtropical climates due to the weathering of rocks rich in aluminium.
 
• India is among the top producers of bauxite in the world, with Odisha being the leading state in bauxite production.
 
 
 
• **National Aluminium Company Limited (NALCO):**
 
 
• NALCO is one of the largest integrated aluminium producers in Asia.
 
• It operates a 22.75 lakh TPA alumina refinery at Damanjodi, which uses bauxite from the Panchpatmali mines.
 
 
 
• **Aluminium Industry in India:**
 
 
• Aluminium is a vital metal used in industries like aerospace, construction, transportation, and packaging.
 
• India is one of the largest producers of aluminium, with significant contributions from Odisha, Jharkhand, and Chhattisgarh.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Concerns:**
 
 
• The mining of bauxite has environmental implications, such as deforestation and habitat destruction.
 
• Efforts are being made to adopt sustainable mining practices to mitigate these impacts.

questions.question: Tirot Sing was the leader of which of the following revolts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Khasi Uprising**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tirot Sing Syiem** was a chief of the Khasi people and is remembered for his pivotal role in resisting British colonial rule in the early 19th century.
 
• The **Khasi Uprising**, led by Tirot Sing, occurred in the year **1829** as a reaction to British incursions into Khasi territories for building a road connecting Assam and Sylhet.
 
• The revolt was triggered when Tirot Sing realized that the British were infringing upon Khasi sovereignty under the guise of constructing infrastructure.
 
• The Khasi tribes under Tirot Sing employed guerilla warfare to resist the British but were ultimately subdued due to superior British military tactics and resources.
 
• Tirot Sing was captured in **1833** and later died in captivity, symbolizing resistance against colonial oppression in Northeast India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khasi Hills:**

 
 
• The Khasi Hills are located in present-day Meghalaya, forming part of the Khasi-Jaintia Hills region.
 
• The Khasi people are one of the major indigenous ethnic groups in Northeast India, known for their matrilineal society.
 
 
 
• **Causes of the Khasi Uprising:**
 
 
• The British sought to construct a road through Khasi territory to connect **Guwahati (Assam)** with **Sylhet (now in Bangladesh)**.
 
• This was seen as an attempt to undermine the sovereignty of the Khasi chiefs.
 
 
 
• **Methods of Resistance:**
 
 
• The Khasis employed **guerrilla tactics**, using the hilly terrain to their advantage against British forces.
 
• The revolt was part of a broader pattern of localized tribal uprisings in India during the 19th century.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Tirot Sing:**
 
 
• Tirot Sing is a revered figure in Meghalaya, celebrated as a hero of resistance against colonial rule.
 
• His death anniversary is observed as a state holiday in Meghalaya, commemorating his fight for Khasi autonomy.

questions.question: ________ dance is embedded in the stories from the epics Mahabharata, Ramayana and Puranas.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathakali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kathakali** is a **classical dance-drama **from Kerala that depicts stories from the **Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Puranas**.
 
• It originated in the 16th century AD and is rooted in earlier forms like **Ramanattam** and **Krishnanattam**.
 
• The dance form combines acting, dance, and music to narrate mythological tales with **elaborate costumes and facial expressions**.
 
• Each performance is expressive and symbolic, using **mudras (hand gestures)** and facial movements to convey emotions and dialogues.
 
• Kathakali is traditionally performed in temples and cultural festivals, often continuing from dusk till dawn.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ramanattam and Krishnanattam**

 
 
• Both are 17th-century Sanskrit plays based on the lives of Rama and Krishna respectively.
 
• Kathakali evolved by incorporating elements of these forms, especially dramatic narration and devotional themes.
 
 
 
• **Costume and Makeup**
 
 
• Kathakali performers wear **vivid makeup**, large headgear, and layered costumes to symbolize different characters.
 
• Colors denote character types—green for noble heroes, red for evil, black for forest dwellers or hunters, etc.
 
 
 
• **Music and Instruments**
 
 
• The performance is accompanied by traditional instruments like **chenda**, **maddalam**, **idakka**, and **cymbals**.
 
• Vocalists narrate the story while dancers enact it silently through expressive gestures.
 
 
 
• **Facial Expressions (Navarasas)**
 
 
• Kathakali uses the concept of **Navarasas (nine emotions)** to convey the mental states of characters.
 
• This includes love, humor, anger, sorrow, heroism, fear, disgust, wonder, and peace.

questions.question: The Dravidian style of temple architecture can be largely seen from which part of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Southern India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Dravidian style of temple architecture** is predominantly found in the southern states of India, including Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Kerala.
 
• Prominent examples of Dravidian architecture include **Brihadeeswarar Temple** in Thanjavur, **Meenakshi Temple** in Madurai, and **Ranganathaswamy Temple** in Srirangam.
 
• This style is characterized by **pyramidal towers (Gopurams)**, intricate carvings, and elaborate designs on temple walls and pillars.
 
• The architecture flourished under powerful South Indian dynasties like the **Pallavas, Cholas, Pandyas, and Vijayanagara** rulers.
 
• Key features include **large courtyards, mandapas (pillared halls)**, and water tanks within the temple complex.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dravidian Architecture Features:**

 
 
• Gopurams: Monumental entrance towers that dominate the temple's skyline.
 
• Vimana: The sanctum tower built directly above the sanctum sanctorum.
 
• Carvings: Depictions of deities, mythological stories, and intricate designs.
 
• Use of Granite: Most temples were constructed using durable granite stones.
 
 
 
• **Important Dynasties:**
 
 
• **Pallavas:** Early examples like Kailasanathar Temple in Kanchipuram.
 
• **Cholas:** Known for massive temples like Brihadeeswarar Temple.
 
• **Pandyas:** Contributed to the expansion of temple complexes.
 
• **Vijayanagara Empire:** Famous for temples in Hampi.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• Temples served as cultural and religious centers in South India.
 
• They were integral to social life, facilitating festivals, education, and governance.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites:**
 
 
• The Great Living Chola Temples (e.g., Brihadeeswarar Temple) are recognized as UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

questions.question: In India, who introduced the idea of the poverty line for the first time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadabhai Naoroji**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji** was the first to introduce the concept of the poverty line in India in his book **"Poverty and Un-British Rule in India"**, published in 1901.
 
• He estimated a subsistence-level poverty line based on the cost of a subsistence diet, which he termed the **"breadline"**.
 
• Naoroji's analysis argued that the average annual income of an Indian was insufficient to meet basic needs, highlighting the economic exploitation under British rule.
 
• He calculated the poverty line at **₹16 to ₹35 per capita annually** based on the prevailing prices of that time.
 
• Naoroji's work laid the foundation for future poverty estimation methodologies in India and emphasized the economic drain theory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Poverty Line:**

 
 
• The poverty line is a threshold used to determine the minimum level of income required to meet basic needs such as food, clothing, and shelter.
 
• It is often adjusted for inflation and varies based on regional cost of living and economic conditions.
 
 
 
• **Economic Drain Theory:**
 
 
• Introduced by Dadabhai Naoroji, this theory argued that wealth was being drained from India to Britain during colonial rule through high taxes, trade policies, and administrative expenses.
 
• It served as a strong critique of British economic policies in India and was a significant component of the nationalist movement.
 
 
 
• **Modern Poverty Estimation in India:**
 
 
• Post-independence, methods to estimate poverty were refined by economists such as Dandekar and Rath (1971) and later by the Planning Commission using calorie intake-based measures.
 
• The Tendulkar Committee (2009) and Rangarajan Committee (2014) provided updated methodologies for poverty estimation in India.
 
 
 
• **Current Measurement:**
 
 
• The poverty line in India is currently calculated using multidimensional indicators such as income, education, health, and living standards, aligned with global frameworks like the UNDP's Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI).

questions.question: Layers of varying thickness are found in which type of rock?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2 - Sedimentary rock**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sedimentary rocks** are formed by the accumulation and compression of sediments like sand, silt, and clay over time.
 
• These rocks often display distinct **layers of varying thickness**, called strata, which are a result of different deposition events.
 
• Common examples of sedimentary rocks include **sandstone, shale, limestone, and conglomerate**.
 
• The layering in sedimentary rocks provides valuable insights into **earth's geological history**, including climate, environment, and life forms.
 
• Sedimentary rocks constitute about **75% of the Earth's surface**, making them one of the most common types of rocks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Strata:** The visible layers in sedimentary rocks are called strata, and their thickness can vary significantly depending on the deposition process.
 
• **Formation Process:** Sedimentary rocks are formed through processes such as **weathering, erosion, transportation, deposition, and lithification**.
 
• **Fossils:** Sedimentary rocks often contain **fossils**, providing critical information about past life forms and environments.
 
• **Types of Sedimentary Rocks:** They are categorized into **clastic** (formed from fragments of pre-existing rocks), **chemical** (formed from mineral precipitation), and **organic** (formed from accumulated biological material).
 
• **Economic Importance:** Many sedimentary rocks serve as reservoirs for **water, oil, natural gas, and coal**, making them economically significant.
